complexity.explanation: Interpolation search uses value distribution to estimate position. Best case occurs when guesses are accurate. Average case is O(log log n) for uniformly distributed data. Worst case degrades to O(n) for non-uniform distributions.

description.brief: An advanced searching algorithm that uses value distribution to estimate the target's position, similar to looking up a name in a phone book.
detailed: Algorithm Analysis:
Time Complexity:
• Best case:    O(1)   - perfect guess on first try
• Average case: O(log log n) - for uniformly distributed data
• Worst case:   O(n)   - for non-uniform distributions
Space Complexity: O(1) - constant extra space
Key Characteristics:
• Requires sorted input array
• Uses value interpolation formula
• Works best on uniformly distributed data
• Intuitive - like searching a phone book
• Can be faster than binary search for uniform data
Performance Metrics:
• Comparisons: O(log log n) average
• Memory: Constant O(1) auxiliary space
• Guess Accuracy: Depends on data distribution
Comparison with Other Search Algorithms:
• Binary Search: O(log n) but works on any distribution
• Linear Search: O(n) but simpler
• Jump Search: O(√n) with better cache locality
• Exponential Search: Better for unbounded arrays
